title: Assessment Exam: Matter, Solutions, and Mixtures
description: 20-question comprehensive assessment covering classification of matter, mixture types, density, and molality with advanced UPCAT-style problems.

questions.question: Which substance is correctly classified?
questions.explanation: Diamond is an element (pure substance of only carbon atoms). Glucose is a pure compound (not a mixture); seawater is a mixture; brass is a homogeneous alloy mixture (not a compound).

questions.question: A 250 mL sample of ethanol has a density of 0.789 g/mL. What is its mass?
questions.explanation: Mass = density × volume = 0.789 g/mL × 250 mL = 197.25 g

questions.question: When light passes through a colloid, a visible beam path appears. This phenomenon is called the:
questions.explanation: The Tyndall effect occurs when light scatters off colloidal particles (1 nm-1 μm), making the light path visible. Solutions do not show this effect.

questions.question: A student observes that an unknown mixture does not scatter laser light, settles completely after 10 days, and can be filtered. The mixture is most likely a:
questions.explanation: Suspensions settle within days/hours and can be filtered. The fact that it settles (not a solution or colloid) and can be filtered (particles > 1 μm) confirms it is a suspension.

questions.question: Which pair correctly distinguishes a solution from a colloid?
options: Solutions are opaque; colloids are transparent
Solutions have particles <1 nm; colloids have particles 1 nm-1 μm
Solutions can be filtered; colloids cannot
Solutions settle quickly; colloids do not settle
questions.explanation: Particle size is the key distinction: solutions have particles <1 nm, while colloids have particles 1 nm-1 μm. Solutions are transparent, colloids are opaque. Neither settles quickly, and neither can be filtered easily.

questions.question: A liquid X has a density of 1.26 g/mL, and liquid Y has a density of 0.88 g/mL. If equal volumes of X and Y are mixed, which will tend to sink to the bottom?
options: Liquid X, because it is denser
Liquid Y, because it is less dense
Cannot be determined without knowing their masses
questions.explanation: The denser liquid (X, with 1.26 g/mL) will sink to the bottom when mixed with the less dense liquid (Y, 0.88 g/mL). Density determines buoyancy.

questions.question: Calculate the molality of a solution made by dissolving 29.25 g of NaCl (molar mass = 58.5 g/mol) in 1000 g of water.
questions.explanation: Moles of NaCl = 29.25 g / 58.5 g/mol = 0.5 mol; Mass of water = 1000 g = 1.0 kg; Molality = 0.5 mol / 1.0 kg = 0.5 m

questions.question: Why is molality preferred over molarity for colligative property calculations?
options: Molality is independent of temperature changes
Molarity cannot be used for colligative properties
questions.explanation: Molality depends only on mass (moles/kg solvent), which does not change with temperature. Molarity (moles/L solution) changes with temperature as solutions expand or contract. For colligative properties, which depend on the number of dissolved particles, molality provides consistent values across temperature ranges.

questions.question: Which statement about the Tyndall effect is correct?
options: It occurs in solutions because particles scatter light
It is used to distinguish suspensions from colloids
It occurs in colloids because particles are large enough to scatter light
It proves that a mixture is homogeneous
questions.explanation: The Tyndall effect occurs in colloids (particles 1 nm-1 μm) because they are large enough to scatter light. Solutions do not show it (particles <1 nm too small). Suspensions do not show obvious Tyndall effects.

questions.question: True or False: A substance that floats in water must have a density less than 1.0 g/mL.
questions.explanation: True. Objects float when their density is less than the medium's density. Since water has a density of 1.0 g/mL, anything floating in it must have a density < 1.0 g/mL.

questions.question: True or False: Compounds are pure substances, but mixtures are not.
questions.explanation: True. Pure substances include elements and compounds. Mixtures are physical combinations of pure substances and are not considered pure substances because their composition can vary.

questions.question: True or False: Blood is a solution because it appears to be a liquid.
questions.explanation: False. Although blood appears liquid, it is a colloid and heterogeneous mixture containing suspended cells (red blood cells, white blood cells, platelets) in plasma.

questions.question: True or False: All elements are pure substances.
questions.explanation: True. Elements are pure substances consisting of only one type of atom. They cannot be decomposed into simpler substances by ordinary chemical means.

questions.question: A 100 mL sample of liquid mercury has a mass of 1360 g. Its density is _____ g/mL.
questions.explanation: Density = mass/volume = 1360 g / 100 mL = 13.6 g/mL

questions.question: How many moles of glucose (molar mass = 180 g/mol) are in 45 g of glucose? _____ mol
questions.explanation: Moles = mass / molar mass = 45 g / 180 g/mol = 0.25 mol

questions.question: A solution is prepared by dissolving 20 g of KBr (molar mass = 119 g/mol) in 250 g of water. The molality is _____ m.
questions.explanation: Moles of KBr = 20 g / 119 g/mol = 0.168 mol; Mass of water = 250 g = 0.25 kg; Molality = 0.168 mol / 0.25 kg = 0.672 m ≈ 0.671 m

questions.question: A block of wood with a mass of 80 g displaces 100 mL of water when submerged. Its density is _____ g/mL.
questions.explanation: Density = mass/volume = 80 g / 100 mL = 0.8 g/mL

questions.question: Explain the difference between a homogeneous mixture and a heterogeneous mixture, and provide one example of each.
acceptableAnswers: Homogeneous mixtures have uniform composition and appear as a single phase (e.g., saltwater, sugar solution, air). Heterogeneous mixtures have non-uniform composition with visibly distinct components (e.g., oil and water, sand and gravel, muddy water).
Homogeneous: uniform throughout (solution/colloid); Heterogeneous: visibly distinct phases (suspension). Example homogeneous: saltwater. Example heterogeneous: sand+water.
questions.explanation: Homogeneous mixtures appear uniform under normal observation and are single-phase. Heterogeneous mixtures show distinct components and multiple phases. Solutions and colloids are homogeneous; suspensions are heterogeneous.

questions.question: A chemist has three samples: pure water, saltwater solution, and milk. Describe a procedure using the Tyndall effect to distinguish between them.
acceptableAnswers: Shine a laser pointer through each sample. Pure water and saltwater (solution) will not show a visible laser beam path (no Tyndall effect). Milk (colloid) will show a bright, visible beam due to light scattering by fat globules. This distinguishes the colloid from the solution and pure liquid.
Direct a laser beam through each. Milk will show the Tyndall effect (visible beam); water and saltwater will not. This differentiates the colloid from solutions.
questions.explanation: The Tyndall effect is visible in colloids (milk) but not in solutions (saltwater) or pure liquids (water). This provides a simple, direct method to distinguish mixture types.
